mode: read-only source and evidence review; no code or tests changed

result.root_is: per-entry provenance for an observation, not currently part of the public stable finding identity contract
result.bug_class: Confirmed implementation behavior loses a distinct synthetic root attribution. Whether this is a contract mismatch or intentional sink-level aggregation is unresolved because the reviewed public schema/identity contract does not require root provenance and no explicit first-root-only contract was found.
must_not_conflate: Same root, two branch/path observations at one sink are intentionally coalesced to one sink finding.
Two distinct roots reaching one source-backed helper sink produce one sink finding but currently retain only one root's attribution.

analysis_observation.meaning: root_key is explicit per-observation provenance; it identifies the active entry root as (root.file, root.qualified).

interpreter_run_dedup.behavior: setdefault keeps the first observation; trace, root_key, entry_grade, dispatch_note, impact basis, and descriptor identity are not part of the key or merged into the retained value.

public_finding.behavior: DetectorFinding is constructed from the retained observation's sink fields, message, and obligations. root_key itself is not serialized as a finding field. Entry grade and root path can affect the generated dispatch/build-membership evidence obligations, so first-root-wins can change the review evidence presented.

layered_identity_contract.behavior: Stable semantic identity is repository + rule_lineage_id + symbol_identity + ast_fingerprint; occurrence identity describes a source occurrence. Root is not a required identity component and IPC findings do not presently export a root provenance set.
layered_identity_contract.implication: Do not add root to semantic finding identity merely to preserve attribution; that would incorrectly create separate findings for one shared sink. Preserve a sink-level finding with a set of root provenance records.

establishment.summary: _entry_roots collects eligible allowlisted IPC dispatchers, named inner/service/transport entries and unique source-index dispatch bindings. It deduplicates roots by (file, qualified function). Test-only roots are skipped and recorded.

walk_and_emit.summary: run iterates roots in discovered function/index order, sets self.root for each walk, and direct/helper analysis emits an Observation carrying the active root. Source-backed helper bodies are walked with the caller root retained. Multiple roots can therefore create distinct observations at the same helper sink.

resolution_boundary.same_file: Resolution prefers a unique matching owner/name in the current file. Ambiguous matches stay unresolved.
resolution_boundary.cross_file: Ordinary helper resolution requires an explicitly qualified callee, a matching owner (or its supported short owner form), and a unique definition; receiver calls on unknown objects are not resolved. Delegated service calls require a source-backed typed/singleton receiver and a unique target.
resolution_boundary.scope_note: The T61 shared-helper oracle uses two explicitly allowlisted roots and one source-backed helper in one synthetic source file. It proves coalescer behavior for that supported shape; it does not show an actual product component has a helper shared by multiple roots. A cross-file variant may be reachable only through the bounded qualified/delegated resolution paths and was not independently demonstrated in T61.

strongest_counterexample.fixture: T61 synthetic_multi_root_oracle: Foo::OnRemoteRequest and Bar::OnRemoteRequest both call one Helper::copy(MessageParcel&) containing one DATA-01 sink; both roots are explicitly allowlisted.
strongest_counterexample.why_strong: Both roots are distinct and explicitly selected, both traverse the same source-backed helper sink, while the sink identity is identical. The final record cannot tell that a second entry path was analyzed; current setdefault order chooses which root's path/obligations survive.
strongest_counterexample.most_material_consequence_example: If two otherwise same-key roots have different entry grades (allowlist versus dispatch), the dropped root may carry the dispatch evidence obligation; if one root is a test-only source path and another is product-like, root-derived build-membership evidence may likewise depend on traversal order. This is a contract-level counterexample, not proof either shape exists in product.

assessment.is_root_part_of_source_observation_ident: The implementation records root_key as provenance on each source observation, so yes for provenance/coverage attribution. The public finding identity/schema reviewed does not make root a required semantic or occurrence identity component.
assessment.is_loss_bug_or_expected_aggregation: Sink-level aggregation is expected. Loss of distinct root provenance is confirmed behavior, but a confirmed contract mismatch is NOT established: the public schema/identity contract does not require root attribution, and no explicit decision documents first-root-only semantics. This needs an owner decision on whether root provenance must survive aggregation.
assessment.actual_product_shared_helper: unknown; the synthetic witness is not product reachability evidence, and no product call graph was audited for this exact many-roots-to-one-helper topology.
assessment.security_impact: None established. This affects potential evidence fidelity/review obligations only if root-specific obligations are required; no contract violation or vulnerability is proven.

minimal_fix_design.preferred: Keep the coalescing key (file,line,rule,symbol) for one sink finding, but aggregate provenance on collision. Add an immutable root-provenance collection to Observation (or an internal grouped observation) containing distinct root_key, entry_grade, dispatch_note, and root-derived evidence flags; union it deterministically when the sink key collides.
minimal_fix_design.public_contract: If downstream reviewers need the data, expose a versioned optional provenance array/sidecar field on DetectorFinding/report output. Keep legacy diagnostic IDs and semantic finding identity unchanged. Preserve existing single-root behavior and avoid fabricating path-specific trace equivalence; retain one deterministic representative trace and explicitly mark/omit trace as complete for all roots.
minimal_fix_design.obligations: Derive obligations from the aggregate of contributing roots: include dispatch/build-membership obligations whenever any contributing root requires them. Do not let whichever root happens to be visited first decide the obligations.
minimal_fix_design.fallback_if_schema_change_deferred: Internally merge root-derived obligations and add a focused test; document that only representative trace is retained. This fixes review gating but still leaves root names unavailable to external consumers.
minimal_fix_design.avoid: Do not add root_key to the dedup key as a first fix: it would turn one shared sink into multiple findings, increase candidate counts, produce duplicate alerts, and alter public compatibility. Do not union branch traces blindly into one path trace.

compatibility_and_count_effects.preferred_aggregate: No finding-count increase: two-root fixture remains one sink finding. Existing single-root output is unchanged. New optional provenance is additive; schema/version consumers need unknown-field tolerance or a versioned sidecar.
compatibility_and_count_effects.root_in_key_alternative: Would increase count from 1 to 2 in T61 multi-root synthetic case and generally duplicate sink alerts across roots; may alter stable/occurrence identity and downstream suppression/grouping. Not recommended.
compatibility_and_count_effects.unrelated_existing_semantics: Current run-level behavior also selects one representative message/trace and may select root-derived evidence obligations by root iteration order. Root aggregation should avoid changing distinct sink line/rule identities.

recommended_regression_oracle.same_root_branch_paths: Two branch observations at one sink, same root: one finding, one distinct provenance root.
recommended_regression_oracle.two_roots_shared_helper: Two roots with distinct root keys reach one same-file helper sink: one finding, provenance includes both roots exactly once; obligations are unioned independent of root order.
recommended_regression_oracle.cross_file_supported_case: Unique explicitly-qualified helper in a second file reached by two roots: same aggregation assertion, if the parser fixture can exercise current supported resolution.
recommended_regression_oracle.order_independence: Reverse root/function order: sink count, provenance set and obligations remain identical; representative trace is either canonicalized or explicitly scoped to its root.
